conversation:
Selina: The volunteers painted the school walls for free, but the colour is a bit dull.
Habib: We didn't have any budget at all. Bhikkhar chal kanra ar akanra.
correct: Habib says they can't be choosy about work done for free.
literal: Rice given to a beggar can be either husked or still in its husk.
plausible: Habib wants the volunteers to repaint the walls in a brighter colour.

meaning_en: Two people or things that are too different can't get along.
conversation:
Debosmita: My father is a die-hard Mohun Bagan fan and my father-in-law is East Bengal to the bone. Every family dinner ends in a fight.
Farhan: Tele jole mish khay na.
correct: The two fathers are far too different ever to get along.
literal: Oil and water simply cannot mix, however long you stir them together.
plausible: Farhan thinks the two fathers secretly enjoy their dinner fights.

meaning_en: A bad person always finds an excuse.
conversation:
Tamal: My colleague missed the deadline again. First it was the Wi-Fi, now it's a 'family function'.
Raisa: Durjoner chholer obhab hoy na.
correct: Someone like him will always come up with another excuse.
literal: A wicked man never runs short of excuses, as if he keeps a stock of them.
plausible: Raisa thinks the colleague's Wi-Fi really was broken that week.

proverb_bn: কাঁচায় না নোয়ালে বাঁশ, পাকলে করে ট্যাঁশ ট্যাঁশ
romanised: Kanchay na noyale bansh, pakle kore tyansh tyansh.
meaning_en: Discipline and habits must be taught when young.
conversation:
Kamal: We let our son skip namaz and homework when he was little. Now at twenty he listens to no one.
Rahela: Kanchay na noyale bansh, pakle kore tyansh tyansh.
correct: Discipline should have been taught when the son was young.
literal: Bamboo that is not bent while it is green will crack once it is fully grown.
plausible: Rahela thinks the son will start listening once he marries.

meaning_en: Wasting effort or resources on something useless.
conversation:
Jamil: The ministry keeps funding that factory, though it hasn't produced anything for ten years.
Sufia: Bhoshme ghi dhala.
correct: The ministry is wasting money on something completely useless.
literal: The ministry keeps pouring precious ghee onto a pile of dead ashes.
plausible: Sufia thinks the factory will start producing again soon.

proverb_bn: সাধে কি বাবা বলি, গুঁতোর চোটে বাবা বলি
romanised: Shadhe ki baba boli, gunttor chote baba boli.
meaning_en: Showing respect only because one is forced to.
conversation:
Kibria: Why do you keep praising the union leader on Facebook? You hate him.
Rajon: He decides who gets the overtime. Shadhe ki baba boli, gunttor chote baba boli.
correct: Rajon praises the leader only because he is forced to.
literal: He calls him father not out of love but because of the jabs.
plausible: Rajon has truly come to like the union leader after all this time.

meaning_en: Unequal treatment for people in the same situation.
conversation:
Parijat: Both of us were late by the same ten minutes, but only I got a warning letter. Rohit got a smile.
Swagatika: Ek jatray prithok phol.
correct: Parijat was punished while Rohit, just as late, was not.
literal: Two people on the same journey ended up with different results.
plausible: Swagatika thinks Rohit had a good excuse for coming late.
